mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPI growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous three months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the previous month signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% over the previous month signals weakening supply-side activity, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) growth is below 1% annualized over the previous month, it signals a mismatch between monetary policy and inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the interaction effect between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the previous month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the interaction effect between PAYEMS and UNRATE on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous two months signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, which boosts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances with increased HOUST, or if the correlation between HOUST growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.25% over the previous month, it signals a restrictive monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
